edition: Issue #010 - A halfback says I'll be back, a 68-year-old icon out-awards Taylor Swift, and Bezos parks his $800m boat in the harbour
tagline: Your 3-minute break. Zero fluff, maximum banter.

stories.headline: Nathan Cleary posts from his hospital bed: I'll be back - and begs fans to lay off the bloke who hurt him
stories.summary: After a compound fracture ended Penrith star Nathan Cleary's season, he told fans to stop harassing the tackler who landed on him - meanwhile the NRL judiciary decides Phoenix Crossland's grand final fate on Tuesday.

body.text: Penrith Panthers halfback Nathan Cleary had his 2026 season ended on Sunday when he suffered a horrific compound fracture of his left ankle during the NRL preliminary final loss to Newcastle. On Monday he posted a photo from hospital - leg bandaged, smiling, thumbs up - with the caption Surgery done and I'll be back. Cleary had started the game from the bench already playing with a broken bone in his right foot, came on 25 minutes into the first half, and lasted only ten minutes before Newcastle hooker Phoenix Crossland fell on his ankle in a tackle that saw Crossland sent off and referred to the NRL judiciary, which sits on Tuesday to decide whether he can play in next weekend's grand final.

The actual winner of this photo is whoever decided a man with a freshly compound-fractured ankle should be giving a thumbs up like he just won a meat raffle. And here is the part that makes you feel oddly warm about professional sport: the bloke whose season just got folded in half is now spending his hospital bedtime telling strangers to stop being awful to the tackler who did it. Sir has just been handed the most generous excuse in the world to be a grump, and he has chosen spread love not hate. Meanwhile the man who may have cost Newcastle their first grand final in 25 years is clinging to the hope that the judiciary has watched a replay and developed a heart.

RNZ/ABC News (29 Sep 2026, Simon Smale): Cleary, 28, suffered a compound fracture of his left ankle in Penrith's 22-14 loss to Newcastle in the NRL preliminary final on 27 September 2026, after leading 14-6 at half-time, ruling him out of the Kangaroos' World Cup campaign. He was already carrying a broken bone in his right foot. Phoenix Crossland was sent off for a hip-drop and referred to the NRL judiciary, which sits on Tuesday; a lengthy ban could also rule him out of the Kiwis' World Cup campaign. Cleary publicly asked people to stop abusing Crossland, who he said had apologised. Former Maroons coach Billy Slater, on his podcast, argued current tackle-interpretation rules left tacklers in passive positions. Newcastle reach their first NRL grand final in 25 years against the Sydney Roosters.

stories.headline: Madonna beats Taylor Swift at the MTV VMAs - and the 68-year-old's maths wins the night
stories.summary: Madonna took Artist of the Year and three trophies total, led nominations for the first time in 28 years, and still lost the story to Swift, who won Video of the Year with her record 31st VMA.

body.text: At the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards in Los Angeles, Madonna took home three trophies including Artist of the Year, while Taylor Swift left with two - one of them the night's biggest prize, Video of the Year for The Fate of Ophelia. Madonna led the nominations for the first time in 28 years, her 13 nods beating Swift's 11, and opened the show with Sabrina Carpenter before winning Best Collaboration and Best Dance. Swift also won the inaugural Artist Director Honors, moving her past Beyonce to a record 31 career VMAs, and used the moment to premiere her new video Patient Zero featuring Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell. Snoop Dogg hosted and, in true Snoop fashion, promised the biggest party in VMA history and some sticky-icky for the winners.

A 68-year-old woman just out-hustled the self-described most powerful woman in entertainment at an awards show, and the headline is still asking whether the 68-year-old beat anyone. Wine aunt supremacy: Madge led nominations for the first time since the Clinton administration and still had time to win an award for a song called Bring Your Love, which is exactly what a woman who has been doing this since before most of the audience was born calls a comeback. Taylor fans, relax - she walked away with the actual video trophy and a record nobody can touch for a while. And Snoop promising weed to winners while telling everyone else to check under their seats is the closest any awards show has come to a productivity seminar. Everyone wins at the VMAs; some people just win with more sticky-icky.

RNZ/ABC News (28 Sep 2026): At the MTV Video Music Awards at the Peacock Theater in LA on 27 September 2026, Madonna won Artist of the Year, Best Dance and (with Sabrina Carpenter) Best Collaboration, taking three trophies on a night she led nominations for the first time in 28 years with 13 nods to Swift's 11. Taylor Swift won Video of the Year for The Fate of Ophelia and the inaugural Artist Director Honors, moving her to a record 31 career VMAs, one clear of Beyonce; she premiered the video for Patient Zero starring Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell. Snoop Dogg hosted. The show discontinued the Best Rock Video award and honoured Nirvana (Vanguard Award), George Michael and Dolly Parton.

stories.headline: Jeff Bezos parks his $800m superyacht Koru in Auckland - and yes, it's called Koru
stories.summary: One of the largest sailing yachts in the world, the 127m Koru worth around $800m NZD, arrived in Auckland this morning with a separate 75m support vessel that carries a helipad.

body.text: One of the largest sailing yachts in the world, owned by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, arrived in Auckland this morning. The three-masted superyacht Koru, built by Oceanco in the Netherlands, is 127m long and 17m wide and reportedly worth US$500 million (about $800m NZD). Marine Traffic tracked it travelling south in the Hauraki Gulf around 6.20am. Koru carries up to 18 guests and needs a crew of about 40, and travels with a separate 75m support vessel, Abeona, which is equipped with a helipad and hangar. A Port of Auckland spokesperson said they were not in a position to comment on the yacht's whereabouts or plans.

Good news for anyone who has ever described their own week as a lot: somewhere out there a man needs 40 people and a separate 75-metre boat with a helicopter just to go on holiday. Koru means new beginnings, which is adorable, but the only new thing beginning in Auckland Harbour this morning is a local council meeting about marine traffic. And let us be honest about the optics - a vessel named for a sacred Maori symbol of renewal worth more than most suburbs, parked in the Waitemata. We are not anti-boat. We are anti-boat-that-costs-more-than-a-suburb-appearing-with-forty-crew-while-Kiwis-scan-the-menu-for-prices. Everyone deserves a holiday; most of us just accept that ours does not come with its own helicopter hangar.

NZ Herald (29 Sep 2026): Jeff Bezos' superyacht Koru, one of the largest sailing yachts in the world, was due to arrive in Auckland on the morning of 29 September 2026, tracked south in the Hauraki Gulf around 6.20am. Built by Oceanco (Netherlands), Koru is 127m long, 17m wide, reportedly worth US$500 million (about $800m NZD), accommodates up to 18 guests and requires about 40 crew; it sails with a 75m support vessel, Abeona, carrying equipment, tenders, a helipad and hangar. Bezos acquired the yacht, named after the Maori koru symbol of new beginnings, in 2023. A Port of Auckland spokesperson declined to comment on the vessel's whereabouts or plans.
